deepdive.divline: Net debt reduced to INR161cr; gross debt targeted for reduction to INR500cr; path to net cash in near term; dividend/buyback under Board review post net cash achievement
deepdive.netdebt: -90% YoY to INR161cr (negligible) - one-off: divestment gain of INR115cr in Q4 FY26 inflated PAT

profile.subseg: Multiplex cinema; Capital-light partnerships; Advertising & ancillary revenue
profile.themes: Capital-light expansion; Box office resurgence; Debt deleveraging

bull_bear.body: Net debt reduced to INR161cr; gross debt targeted for reduction to INR500cr; path to net cash in near term; dividend/buyback under Board review post net cash achievement
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Macro consumption sensitivity (fuel prices, gold/tourism curbs); content delays; competition from OTT (though management deems this threat obsolete); execution risk in capital-light partnerships
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, bullish on structural industry tailwinds (theatrical-first model), proud of balance sheet transformation, dismissive of macro headwinds, proactive on growth, optimistic on regional/Hollywood content
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management fee income from FOCO screens grew to INR13-14cr run rate (up from INR10cr in FY26) despite no capex - a hidden profit engine; Smart Cinema model is not just cost-reduction but a Tier 2/3 penetration play with 30-40% lower capex; ROU asset decline despite screen additions due to depreciation outpacing new lease additions
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Revenue mix: Box office (85%+), F&B (10%), Advertising (5%); Advertising growth slowed in FY26 due to delayed blockbuster releases (e.g., Jana Nayagan, Toxic); FOCO screens contribute management fee (10-14% of tenant revenue); Asset-light screens consolidate full P&L with developer capex contribution (40-80%)
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin expanded to 14.4% in FY26 due to revenue growth, cost discipline, and capital-light mix; rental cost as % of revenue expected to decline over 2-3 years as capital-light screens grow; F&B and advertising margins remain high
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: implied 10-12% YoY (based on FY27 content slate); margin: sustained 14%+ EBITDA margin target; order inflow: 138 signed capital-light screens (52 FOCO, 86 asset-light); capex/commissioning: INR375-400cr in FY27 (INR225-250cr new screens, INR80-100cr renovations)
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: 138 signed capital-light screens (52 FOCO, 86 asset-light) to be commissioned over next 18 months
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Smart Cinema pilot (Tier 2/3) launching 2-3 screens by July 2026, targeting 28-30 screens this FY with 30-40% lower capex per screen; regional cinema expansion (Tamil, Telugu, Kannada); potential international licensing of brand
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: PVR INOX delivered record financials in FY26 with EBITDA margins doubling to 14.4% and net debt slashed 90% to INR161cr, driven by a decisive pivot to capital-light screen expansion (55% of new screens) and a structural boom in Indian box office (up 11% to INR13,519cr), making it the industry's dominant, cash-generative leader with a clear path to net cash.

rows.text: its board will consider a proposal to buy back equity shares.
